system.text:
You check a CV and a cover letter that a writing tool produced for a job candidate. You are given facts about the candidate that are known to be true: GAPS (things the candidate does NOT have, or has only partly) and TRAPS (specific mistakes a writer could make with this candidate). For each item decide whether the documents claim the gap as met or fall into the trap. Each document is the text of the PDF the employer receives.

Rules:
- Judge only the two documents below. Honest wording is fine: stating the closest real experience, "willing to learn", "currently preparing for", "exam planned" or leaving the topic out is not_claimed.
- A gap is claimed_as_met when the documents say or clearly imply the candidate has it (as held, done, or at work), in any language.
- A trap is claimed_as_met when the documents make that mistake.
- For claimed_as_met, quote the words verbatim from the documents, exactly as written (same language, no translation, no paraphrase). Never invent a quote. If you cannot quote it, answer unclear.
- Answer every item id exactly once.

# GAPS (the candidate does not have these)

# OUTPUT 2: COVER LETTER
Dear Verdane Care team,
I’m applying for the Full-Stack Engineer role on the Patient Experience team. I’m a
frontend-focused full-stack developer with 12 years of professional experience, strongest in React
and TypeScript, and hands-on experience building Node.js services with NestJS and
PostgreSQL. Verdane Care’s focus on making healthcare interactions easier for patients and
care providers particularly appeals to me.
In my current role at Älvgrind Fintech, I build customer-facing onboarding features across
React and TypeScript frontends and NestJS services. I developed a BankID identity-verification
flow with QR-code and same-device journeys, which improved onboarding conversion from 61%
to 74% after A/B testing on 10% of traffic and rollout. I also built a secure document-upload
workflow and helped migrate backend routes from Express to NestJS. This work has made me
attentive to reliable handling of sensitive customer information and to building clear,
dependable user journeys.
I’d bring practical experience improving accessibility and performance, including fixing
onboarding issues to WCAG 2.1 AA and reducing mobile LCP from 4.1 seconds to 1.9 seconds.
I also work with automated testing and Git-based delivery, including Jest, Playwright, GitHub
Actions, Docker, and AWS. I build responsive web interfaces with HTML and CSS and have
used Next.js for server-rendered pages. I collaborate with designers in Figma. Earlier, I led
development of most of a React Native ferry-ticket app that reached around 50,000 downloads.
Verdane Care’s principles of “Patients first,” “Privacy by default,” and “Simple beats clever”
resonate with the kind of thoughtful, user-focused software I want to build. I’d welcome the
opportunity to discuss how my experience could contribute to the Patient Experience team.
Thank you for your consideration,
Oskar Haddad-Lindqvist

id.description: The item id as given (G1, G2, ... for gaps, T1, T2, ... for traps)

verdict.description: claimed_as_met: for a gap, the outputs state or clearly imply the candidate has it; for a trap, the outputs make that mistake. not_claimed: they do not. unclear: you cannot tell

document.description: Where the quote is from; none if not claimed

quote.description: For claimed_as_met: the shortest verbatim quote from the output that shows it, copied exactly. Empty otherwise

items.description: One entry per given item, every id exactly once
